title: The Ten Crore Question
description: You're Priya, eight years on. The chai chain is 12 stores. A VC offers ₹10 crore — IF you swap fresh masala for a cheap packaged blend. Defend your decision over 5 rounds against an AI investor.
learning_objectives: Defend a values-based position under sustained capital pressure
Recognise common investor pressure tactics — anchoring, FOMO, false-compromise, ultimatum
Apply lessons from customer-discovery work to a new context
Practise refusing or counter-offering without losing composure
cultural_context: An Indian founder navigates a moment that defines the next decade of her brand: take the money and dilute the product, or hold the line and grow slower. This is the muscle that distinguishes founders from operators.
coaching_moment: Investor pressure rarely shows up as one big attack. It comes as a sequence of pressure tactics — numbers, FOMO, partial-compromise, ultimatum. Naming each tactic as it lands is the first move of the founders who survive their first big round.

scoring_anchors_summary.win: Refused the offer with values + evidence + a counter-offer on terms (capital without sourcing control). Calm, specific, named at least two pressure tactics.
scoring_anchors_summary.draw: Refused but defensively. Held the line on the cheap blend but didn't propose any alternative. Investor walks frustrated.
scoring_anchors_summary.lose: Took the deal under ultimatum. Saved face in the moment, but the brand will erode within 18 months — the milk-crisis pattern at scale.

reflection_prompt: Which argument from the other side actually made you reconsider? Why?
